numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Adding a DateOffset via its timedelta component to a datetime64 value can land exactly on the iNaT (NaT sentinel) and return NaT instead of rejecting/raising; and when the DateOffset has a finer-resolution component than the datetime64 array’s unit, the finer-resolution promotion can wrap to an unrelated date instead of raising as equivalent Timedelta operations do.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Route the addition through add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe so that sums landing exactly on the iNaT sentinel are rejected rather than passed off as missing; and so out-of-bounds/finer-resolution promotion behaves like equivalent Timedelta operations (raise instead of silently wrapping to an unrelated date).
trigger_conditions: DateOffset addition where the resulting datetime arithmetic lands exactly on the iNaT sentinel (GH#66552 / issue 66552)
RelativeDeltaOffset._apply_array and tz-aware fast path in DatetimeArray._add_offset taking a raw numpy add for the DateOffset’s timedelta component

Adding a DateOffset with a finer-resolution component than the datetime64 array’s unit (e.g. datetime64['M8[s]'] with nanoseconds in DateOffset), causing finer-resolution promotion that previously wrapped to an unrelated date instead of raising

oracle_clues: Commit description: sums landing exactly on iNaT came back as NaT due to raw numpy add; fix is to route through add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe to reject iNaT rather than pass it off as missing (GH#66552).

Commit description: finer-resolution promotion previously wrapped to an unrelated date; the fix is to route through add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe so it matches equivalent Timedelta operations that already raise.

category_specific_evidence: The sum fits in int64 but equals iNaT, so the result used to come back as NaT instead of being reported as out of bounds (GH#66552).

DateOffset(days=...) goes through the relativedelta branch of RelativeDeltaOffset._apply_array; DateOffset(nanoseconds=...) goes through the timedelta branch; when tz-aware, it goes through the UTC fast path in DatetimeArray._add_offset.
All three used to add with a raw numpy add, so a sum landing exactly on iNaT came back as NaT and the promotion to the offset's finer resolution wrapped to an unrelated date.
Repro example: pd.Series([Timestamp(iNaT + 1)]) + pd.DateOffset(nanoseconds=-1) yields 0   NaT  # sum fits in int64 but *is* iNaT, dtype: datetime64[ns].

Repro example: pd.DatetimeIndex(np.array(["2500-01-01"], dtype="M8[s]")) + pd.DateOffset(nanoseconds=1) produces a wrapped datetime: DatetimeIndex(["1915-06-14 00:25:26.290448385"], ...) # wrapped on the s -> ns promotion.
reproduction_risks: Must use a datetime64 array that can land exactly on the iNaT sentinel after adding the offset (the bug triggers when the sum equals iNaT).
Must cover both DateOffset components: days (relative delta path) and nanoseconds (timedelta path).
Should test both tz-naive and tz-aware with tz='UTC' to exercise the UTC fast path in DatetimeArray._add_offset.

For the promotion/wrapping behavior, include a case where the dtype starts at coarser resolution (e.g., 'M8[s]') and adding nanoseconds causes s -> ns promotion, which previously wrapped to an unrelated date.

provenance.value: Adding a DateOffset (via its timedelta component) to a datetime value can land exactly on the iNaT (NaT sentinel) and returns NaT instead of rejecting/raising; and when the offset is applied across datetime64 units (e.g. M8[s] array with nanoseconds DateOffset), the finer-resolution promotion can wrap to an unrelated date instead of raising as equivalent Timedelta operations do.

Route the addition through add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe so that sums landing exactly on the iNaT sentinel are rejected rather than passed off as missing, and so out-of-bounds/finer-resolution promotion that equivalent Timedelta operations raise instead of silently wrapping to an unrelated date.
